_comment: SECURITY FINDINGS POLICY. Operator rule, 2026-09-08.
The blanket rules are not negotiable by an agent:
CRITICAL and HIGH  -- must fix. No acceptance path exists.
MEDIUM             -- situation and posture dependent.
LOW                -- acceptable.
FOR A PRODUCTION RELEASE, every TRACTABLE medium and low is fixed too. The
exception is a medium or low that AN ATTACKER CANNOT REACH given the actual
posture and architecture -- those are allowed, and must be ANNOTATED so the
decision is revisitable rather than forgotten. A release is not blocked on an
unreachable low.
The annotation is what makes this a decision instead of a silence. An
unannotated accepted finding is indistinguishable from a finding nobody
looked at -- the same defect as the stub contract, in a place where it costs
more.

critical.why: no acceptance path. An agent may not annotate its way past a critical.

medium.why: situation and posture dependent. Fix it for a release unless it is genuinely unreachable, and say why.

low.why: acceptable day to day; fixed for a release when tractable

_comment: How a medium or low is accepted. Modelled on the stub contract for the same
reason: a marker with no reason is a way to silence the scanner, and a
reason someone can read is a claim they can disagree with.
REACHABLE must argue from the POSTURE, not from the code being careful.
'input is validated' is a code claim and can regress silently. 'no path
from any network input reaches this argv, and the service binds loopback
only' is an architecture claim, and the architecture is what the operator
reasons about.
acceptance_annotation.example:
# SEC-ACCEPTED: S603 subprocess-without-shell
# SEVERITY: low
# REACHABLE: no — argv is a fixed list plus a repo path from the unit file; no
#            network input reaches it, and the service has no shell
# REVISIT: if this ever takes a path from a webhook body
rules: critical and high may NEVER carry this marker; a scanner finding at those levels is a defect to fix
REACHABLE must state an architectural reason, not that the code is careful
an annotation without all three fields is treated as UNANNOTATED and the finding stands

scanners._comment: Self-hosted only. A scanner that is not installed is REPORTED AS ABSENT, never silently treated as clean -- that is the same lie as a skipped CI job reading as success.

secrets.why: a committed credential is reachable by definition -- it is already published to everyone with repo access
secrets._defect: `--report-path -` does NOT write to stdout: gitleaks creates a file literally named `-` in the working directory and prints only its banner. Parsed from stdout it reports zero secrets for every repo forever, and litters each one with a file called `-`. The scanner substitutes a temp path for {tmpfile}. This config shipped the defect its own policy is meant to catch.

python_sast.note: flake8-bandit is built into ruff as the S rules, so Python SAST comes free with the house lint standard rather than needing a separate scanner

containers.note: present on fleet-ci-base:1 but not on host-a

merge.why: the blanket rule. Everything else is release-time or annotated.

release.why: every tractable medium and low is fixed for a release; an unreachable one is allowed WITH its annotation, and a release is never blocked on it
